title: Omni Lending Security Review - Executive Summary
text: Spearbit Security Review. Omni Lending Protocol. Review window 2023-10-02 to 2023-10-20. Lead researchers: two senior and three associate. Scope: core lending market, interest rate model, oracle adapter and liquidation engine at commit 4f19ac2. Out of scope: the front end, the subgraph and the governance token. Summary of findings by severity. Critical 1. High 3. Medium 7. Low 11. Gas optimisation 14. Informational 9. Total 45. Of the 45 issues raised, 38 were acknowledged and fixed before the re-review, 4 were acknowledged and accepted as a risk, and 3 were disputed by the client. The single critical issue concerns the oracle adapter and is described on page 2.

title: Critical: oracle adapter accepts a stale Chainlink round
text: Issue 5.1.1 Critical. Oracle adapter accepts a stale Chainlink round and never validates the answer. Severity Critical. Likelihood High. Impact High. Context: OracleAdapter.sol lines 84 to 102. Description: latestRoundData is destructured but only the answer element is bound; updatedAt, startedAt, roundId and answeredInRound are discarded with an underscore. There is no heartbeat comparison and no positivity requirement on the answer. If an aggregator halts, or the sequencer on an L2 deployment goes down and comes back, the market prices collateral from the last quote for as long as the outage lasts. Recommendation: require block.timestamp minus updatedAt to be below the feed heartbeat plus a grace period, require the answer to be strictly positive, require answeredInRound to be at least roundId, and on an L2 additionally consult the sequencer uptime feed and reject prices inside the grace window after a restart. Client response: fixed in commit 9ab310c, re-reviewed and confirmed.

title: High severity findings: liquidation and interest accrual
text: Issue 5.2.1 High. Liquidation incentive is a fixed bonus rather than a fraction of the repaid debt, so dust liquidations are profitable and drain the reserve. Recommendation: express the bonus as a share of the notional closed and introduce a minimum close factor. Issue 5.2.2 High. Interest is accrued lazily on user interaction only, so a market with no activity between two rate updates applies the newest rate retroactively to the whole idle period. Recommendation: checkpoint the borrow index on every rate change. Issue 5.2.3 High. The close factor allows a full liquidation of a position only marginally below the threshold, which converts a small price move into a total loss for the borrower and is not required to restore solvency. Recommendation: cap the close factor at fifty percent unless the position is below a deeper insolvency bound.

title: Appendix A: fuzzing campaign and invariants
text: Appendix A. Invariant testing. The review included a stateful fuzzing campaign run with Foundry for 200,000 sequences of up to 40 calls. Invariant 1: the sum of all user borrow balances equals totalBorrows within one wei of rounding. Held. Invariant 2: totalAssets is greater than or equal to totalSupply multiplied by the exchange rate. Held. Invariant 3: no account can end a sequence with a health factor below one and a non zero collateral balance that a liquidator could not seize. Broken, reduced to issue 5.2.1. Invariant 4: the borrow index is monotonically non decreasing. Broken under a rate change with zero elapsed time, reduced to issue 5.2.2. Invariant 5: the reserve balance never decreases outside a governance withdrawal. Held.

title: Cantina Competition Report - Cross Chain Messaging
text: Cantina competition report. Cross chain messaging protocol. Competition window 2024-04-08 to 2024-05-06. 312 registered researchers, 89 submitting, 1,204 submissions received, 61 unique valid findings after deduplication. Scope: the message outbox and inbox, the validator attestation library, the fee quoting module and the executor. The judging panel applied a duplicate policy under which the earliest submission demonstrating the root cause takes the primary award. Severity distribution of unique valid findings: Critical 2, High 6, Medium 18, Low 35. The two critical findings both concern replay protection and are summarised on the following page.

title: Critical: message replay across chains and across redeployments
text: Finding C-01 Critical. The attestation digest covers the sender, the recipient, the payload and a nonce, but not the destination chain identifier. A message attested for one destination is accepted verbatim by the inbox on every other chain served by the same validator set. Figure 2 on this page shows the message flow: outbox on chain A emits, validators attest the digest, and three inboxes on chains B, C and D each accept the same attestation. Recommendation: include the destination chain identifier and the inbox address in the signed digest. Finding C-02 Critical. The processed nonce set is stored in the inbox implementation rather than behind the proxy, so an upgrade that changes the implementation address resets replay protection and every historical message becomes replayable. Recommendation: keep the processed set in dedicated proxy storage and cover it with an upgrade migration test.

title: Fee quoting and executor griefing
text: Finding H-03 High. The executor is reimbursed from a fee quoted at send time on the source chain, but the quote is computed from the source chain gas price. When the destination chain gas price rises above the quote the executor makes a loss and rationally stops relaying, and messages stall with no path to top up the fee after the fact. The gas table on this page compares quoted and realised execution cost across five destination chains over the review window; the realised cost exceeded the quote on 18 percent of messages and by more than a factor of three on 2 percent. Recommendation: allow a permissionless fee top up keyed by message identifier, and price the quote from an oracle of destination chain gas rather than from source chain conditions.

title: Judging notes on duplicate clustering
text: Judging methodology. Submissions were clustered by root cause rather than by the affected function, because several distinct entry points reduce to the same missing check. Clustering was performed by two judges independently and disagreements were resolved by a third. Of 1,204 submissions, 71 percent were duplicates of a finding already submitted, 14 percent were out of scope, 9 percent were rejected as informational, and 6 percent were unique valid findings. The mean time from competition open to first submission of each critical finding was 4.2 days, and both critical findings were first reported by researchers who had not audited a bridge previously, which the panel notes as evidence for the value of a broad participant pool.

title: Vault V3 Review - Scope and Methodology
text: Spearbit security review. Vault V3. Review window 2024-07-01 to 2024-07-19. Scope: the ERC-4626 core, the strategy allocator, the withdrawal queue and the fee module at commit b72e004, comprising 3,412 lines of Solidity. Methodology: manual review by three researchers, differential review against the V2 deployment, stateful fuzzing of the share accounting, and a written invariant specification agreed with the client before the review began. Findings: Critical 0, High 2, Medium 5, Low 9, Informational 12. The client had already applied a virtual shares mitigation for the inflation attack before the review, which the reviewers confirmed as correctly implemented on page 3.

title: High: withdrawal queue can be starved by a strategy that reports late
text: Issue 4.1.1 High. The withdrawal queue services requests in order and skips a request it cannot fill from idle assets, but it does not advance a cursor past the skipped entry. A single large request that no single strategy can satisfy therefore blocks every smaller request behind it until an allocator transaction frees enough idle capital, and the allocator is permissioned. Impact: depositors with modest requests cannot exit while one oversized request is pending, which is a liveness failure rather than a loss of funds but is severe under stress. Recommendation: allow partial fulfilment of the head request, or let the queue skip and revisit, and expose a permissionless path that pulls from strategies in a fixed priority order when a request has waited beyond a threshold.

title: Confirmation of the virtual shares inflation mitigation
text: Issue 4.3.2 Informational. Confirmation of the inflation attack mitigation. The vault adds one virtual share and ten to the power of the decimals offset virtual assets inside both conversion functions. We derive the attacker cost for a decimals offset of six: to force a victim depositing d assets to receive zero shares, the attacker must donate at least d multiplied by ten to the power six. For a victim deposit of one thousand units of a six decimal stablecoin the attacker must donate one billion units, so the attack is not economic at any realistic deposit size. The reviewers confirm the mitigation is applied on both the deposit and mint paths and on both the withdraw and redeem paths, and that the offset is immutable after construction.

title: Fee module: performance fee charged on unrealised gains
text: Issue 4.2.3 Medium. The performance fee is assessed against the change in totalAssets since the last accrual, which includes unrealised marks from strategies that value illiquid positions internally. A strategy whose mark rises and then falls back therefore pays a performance fee on a gain that never realised, and the loss is borne by depositors. Worked example: totalAssets rises from 100 to 120 on an unrealised mark, a twenty percent performance fee mints shares worth 4, the mark then reverts to 100, and depositors are left holding 96 units of value against their original 100. Recommendation: apply a high water mark per strategy on realised proceeds only, and exclude marks that a strategy reports as unrealised from the fee base.
